Frequently asked questions

Last updated 1 October 2026

The short version. devildictionary.com is a free word-sliding game of wickedly honest definitions, in the tradition of Ambrose Bierce’s The Devil’s Dictionary (1911). One hundred words hide in letter grids across four stages; find one and the dictionary defines you back. No account, no paywall.

What is devildictionary.com?

devildictionary.com is a free word-sliding game built around The Devil’s Dictionary — a book of wickedly honest definitions in the tradition of Ambrose Bierce’s 1911 classic. You hunt for hidden words in a grid of letters; each word you find unlocks its devilish definition. The tagline says it best: find the word, face the truth.

Is the game free?

Yes. The full game — all 100 entries, all four stages — is completely free to play in your browser. No account, no sign-up, no paywall. There is an optional one-time purchase (Printable Cards, from $2.99) if you want to take the game to your table, but nothing in the game itself costs money.

Do I need an account to play?

No. There are no accounts at all. You just open devildictionary.com and play. Your progress is stored only on your own device, in your browser’s local storage.

How do you play?

Each round hides one dictionary entry in a grid of letters. Hold the first letter and slide across neighbouring cells — rows, columns and diagonals all work — to spell the word. When the word is complete, the dictionary reads its definition back to you.

How many words and stages are there?

100 entries across four stages:

  • Stage I · The Literate — a 5×5 board
  • Stage II · The Doubter — a 6×6 board
  • Stage III · The Accomplice — a 7×7 board
  • Stage IV · The Author — an 8×8 board

Every five entries you complete strikes one Devil Coin — 20 coins in the complete book.

Where do the definitions come from?

Many definitions come from Ambrose Bierce’s The Devil’s Dictionary (1911), which is in the public domain, and the rest were written in that same voice for this game. Quotations from the original are reproduced as published, including period spellings and period opinions.

Who made devildictionary.com?

devildictionary.com was created by Lakeside Harb, an independent maker. New words are published as short videos on X, Instagram and YouTube under the Devil’s Dictionary name.

Is there a book?

Yes. The Devil Defines by Lakeside Harb is available in paperback on Amazon — the game’s definitions collected as a printed book.

What are Printable Cards?

Printable Cards are a one-time purchase (from $2.99) that lets you take the game off-screen: print the word cards and play The Devil’s Dictionary at your table, in classrooms, or at parties.

Is there a mobile app?

The game runs in any modern mobile browser, on iPhone and Android alike, and needs no installation. Progress is stored per device and is never synced between the website and any app.

Where is my progress saved? What if it disappears?

Progress lives only on the device you played on. Clearing site data, using private browsing, or reinstalling an app can erase it — and because nothing is stored on any server, lost progress cannot be recovered. Pressing RESET MY PROGRESS is permanent.

How do I contact support?

Email support@devildictionary.com — for help, corrections, complaints, or simply to argue with a definition.

If that address is masked by a browser extension or an email-privacy filter, it reads: support at devildictionary dot com.
